items.pregunta: My office is on the third ___. I take the lift every morning.
items.explicacion_es: "Floor" significa "piso" de un edificio, y por eso tomas el ascensor para llegar a tu oficina.

items.pregunta: I'm hungry. Can I see the ___, please? I want to order food.
items.explicacion_es: "Menu" es la carta del restaurante; "bill" es la cuenta, que pides al final y no para ordenar comida.

items.pregunta: The meeting is on Friday. Friday is the day after ___.
items.explicacion_es: El viernes (Friday) viene después del jueves, que en inglés es "Thursday".

items.pregunta: It's very cold today. Take your ___.
items.explicacion_es: "Coat" es un abrigo, la prenda que necesitas cuando hace mucho frío.

items.pregunta: I go to work by ___. I wait for it at the station every morning.
items.explicacion_es: Esperas el tren (train) en la estación; además, "a pie" se dice "on foot", no "by foot".

items.pregunta: Excuse me, where is the ___? I want to wash my hands.
items.explicacion_es: "Bathroom" es el baño, el lugar donde te lavas las manos.

items.pregunta: She ___ in a bank.
items.explicacion_es: En presente simple, con he, she e it el verbo lleva "-s": "she works".

items.pregunta: ___ you from Mexico?
items.explicacion_es: Con el verbo "be" y el sujeto "you" se usa "are", y en la pregunta va antes del sujeto: "Are you...?".

items.pregunta: I ___ like tea. I prefer coffee.
items.explicacion_es: Para negar en presente simple con "I" usas "don't" + verbo, no "no" como en español.

items.pregunta: There ___ two printers in the office.
items.explicacion_es: Para decir "hay" con un sustantivo en plural usas "there are", no "have".

items.pregunta: This is Ana. ___ is my manager.
items.explicacion_es: Ana es mujer y funciona como sujeto, así que el pronombre correcto es "she"; "her" no puede ser sujeto.

items.pregunta: The meeting is ___ Monday.
items.explicacion_es: Con los días de la semana se usa la preposición "on": "on Monday".

items.audio_en: Hi, I'm Tom. I'm a teacher and I live in London.
items.pregunta: What is Tom's job?
items.explicacion_es: Tom dice "I'm a teacher", es decir, que es profesor.

items.audio_en: A: What time is the meeting? B: It's at ten thirty.
items.pregunta: When is the meeting?
items.explicacion_es: "Ten thirty" significa las diez y media, es decir, 10:30.

items.audio_en: A: Excuse me, how much is the coffee? B: It's three dollars.
items.pregunta: How much is the coffee?
items.explicacion_es: La persona dice "three dollars", o sea, tres dólares; no confundas "three" con "thirteen" ni con "thirty".

items.audio_en: A: Where is your hotel? B: It's next to the train station.
items.pregunta: Where is the hotel?
items.explicacion_es: La respuesta es "next to the train station", que significa que el hotel está al lado de la estación de tren.

items.pregunta: I'm calling to ___ a table for four people at your restaurant tonight.
items.explicacion_es: Para reservar una mesa en inglés se dice "book a table"; con "make" se diría "make a reservation", no "make a table".

items.pregunta: Our flight was ___ because of the snow, so we left three hours later.
items.explicacion_es: "Delayed" significa retrasado, y es lo que pasa cuando un vuelo sale más tarde de lo previsto.

items.pregunta: Can you ___ me your pen, please? I'll give it back in a minute.
items.explicacion_es: "Lend" es prestar algo a otra persona, mientras que "borrow" es pedir prestado, así que aquí necesitas "lend".

items.pregunta: He never arrives late to meetings. He is very ___.
items.explicacion_es: "Punctual" significa puntual; cuidado con "actual", que en inglés significa real o verdadero.

items.pregunta: I need to ___ some money from the cash machine before we go to the market.
items.explicacion_es: "Take out money" significa sacar dinero de un cajero automático.

items.pregunta: Excuse me, how much does this jacket ___?
items.explicacion_es: Para preguntar el precio de algo se usa "How much does it cost?".

items.pregunta: I ___ to Mexico City last year for a conference.
items.explicacion_es: Con "last year" se usa el pasado simple ("went"), no el presente perfecto.

items.pregunta: This hotel is ___ than the one we stayed in last time.
items.explicacion_es: Los adjetivos cortos como "cheap" forman el comparativo con "-er", sin usar "more".

items.pregunta:
A: What are you doing tomorrow morning?
B: I ___ my manager at 10 o'clock.
items.explicacion_es: Para planes futuros ya organizados se usa el presente continuo: "am" + verbo con "-ing".

items.pregunta: There isn't ___ milk in the fridge. Can you buy some?
items.explicacion_es: En oraciones negativas con sustantivos incontables como "milk" se usa "any".

items.pregunta: We ___ wear a suit to the office. Casual clothes are fine.
items.explicacion_es: "Don't have to" indica que algo no es necesario, mientras que "mustn't" indica que está prohibido.

items.pregunta: I've worked at this company ___ 2019.
items.explicacion_es: Con el presente perfecto se usa "since" + un punto en el tiempo (como un año) y "for" + un período de tiempo.

items.audio_en:
A: Excuse me, where is the meeting room?
B: It's on the second floor, next to the kitchen.
items.pregunta: Where is the meeting room?
opciones: On the first floor, next to the kitchen
On the second floor, next to the kitchen
On the second floor, next to the lift
items.explicacion_es: La persona dice que la sala está en el segundo piso ("second floor"), al lado de la cocina.

items.audio_en: Hi Tom, it's Ana. I'm really sorry, but I can't come to lunch on Friday. Can we meet on Monday instead?
items.pregunta: Why is Ana calling Tom?
opciones: To invite him to lunch for the first time
To say she will be late on Friday
To cancel lunch and suggest another day
items.explicacion_es: Ana dice que no puede ir el viernes y propone verse el lunes en su lugar ("instead").

items.audio_en:
A: How much is a ticket to the airport?
B: A single is eight dollars and a return is fifteen.
A: OK, a return, please.
items.pregunta: How much does the customer pay?
items.explicacion_es: El cliente pide un boleto de ida y vuelta ("return"), que cuesta quince dólares.

items.audio_en: Attention, please. The train to Boston is now leaving from platform six, not platform four. We're sorry for the change.
items.pregunta: Which platform does the train to Boston leave from?
items.explicacion_es: El anuncio dice que el tren sale del andén seis y no del cuatro.

items.pregunta: Could you ___ me a favor and send the report to the client today?
items.explicacion_es: En inglés se dice "do someone a favor", no "make", aunque en español digas "hacer un favor".

items.pregunta: The meeting has been ___ until next Tuesday because the manager is sick.
items.explicacion_es: "Put off" significa posponer, que es lo que pasa con la reunión cuando el gerente está enfermo.

items.pregunta: I thought the hotel would be expensive, but ___ it was quite cheap.
items.explicacion_es: "Actually" significa "en realidad", mientras que "currently" es un falso amigo que significa "actualmente".

items.pregunta: Can I ___ your pen for a moment? I left mine at home.
items.explicacion_es: Usas "borrow" cuando pides algo prestado y "lend" cuando tú le prestas algo a otra persona.

items.pregunta: I'm going to ___ for the job at the bank; the deadline is Friday.
items.explicacion_es: Para postularte a un empleo se dice "apply for a job"; "solicit" es un falso amigo de "solicitar".

items.pregunta: Our customers often ___ about the long waiting times on the phone.
items.explicacion_es: "Complain about" significa quejarse de algo; "claim" no significa "reclamar" en el sentido de quejarse.

items.pregunta: I ___ in this company since 2018.
items.explicacion_es: Con "since" y una acción que continúa hasta hoy se usa el present perfect, no el presente simple como en español.

items.pregunta: If I ___ more time, I would learn Japanese.
items.explicacion_es: En el segundo condicional usas el pasado simple después de "if" y "would" en la otra parte de la oración.

items.pregunta: While I ___ the report, the computer suddenly stopped working.
items.explicacion_es: El past continuous describe una acción en progreso en el pasado que fue interrumpida por otra acción.

items.pregunta: The new products ___ to the store every Monday.
items.explicacion_es: Los productos no entregan nada, sino que son entregados, por eso necesitas la voz pasiva en presente.

items.pregunta: When I was a student, I ___ work in a café on weekends.
items.explicacion_es: "Used to" + verbo expresa un hábito del pasado, mientras que "be used to" significa "estar acostumbrado a".

items.pregunta: I'm looking forward to ___ you at the conference next month.
items.explicacion_es: En "look forward to", "to" es una preposición, así que después va el verbo con -ing.

items.audio_en: Hi Laura, it's Mark from the sales department. The client meeting was supposed to be at ten tomorrow morning, but they asked to move it to the afternoon. Can we meet at two thirty instead? Please call me back before five today.
items.pregunta: What time is the new meeting?
items.explicacion_es: Mark dice que la reunión cambió de las diez a las dos y media de la tarde, y las cinco es la hora límite para devolverle la llamada.

items.audio_en: A: Good evening, I have a reservation under the name Silva. B: Yes, Mr. Silva, a double room for three nights. Breakfast is included and it's served from seven to ten. A: Great. Is there parking at the hotel? B: Yes, but it costs fifteen dollars a day.
items.pregunta: What does the guest have to pay extra for?
items.explicacion_es: El recepcionista dice que el desayuno está incluido, pero que el estacionamiento cuesta quince dólares al día.

items.audio_en: Attention, passengers on flight BA 205 to Madrid. Due to bad weather, the departure has been delayed by about forty-five minutes. The flight will now leave from gate twelve instead of gate eight. We apologize for the inconvenience.
items.pregunta: Apart from the departure time, what has changed?
items.explicacion_es: El anuncio indica que el vuelo ahora sale por la puerta doce en lugar de la ocho.

items.audio_en: A: How was your first week at the new job? B: Not bad. The people are really friendly, but the office is a long way from my house, so I spend almost two hours a day on the bus. A: Could you work from home sometimes? B: Maybe after three months, my manager said.
items.pregunta: What is speaker B's main problem with the new job?
opciones: The manager never allows working from home.
items.explicacion_es: B dice que la oficina está lejos y que pasa casi dos horas al día en el autobús, aunque sus compañeros son amables.

items.pregunta: The negotiations broke down because neither side was willing to ___.
items.explicacion_es: "Compromise" significa ceder en algo para llegar a un acuerdo, que es lo que faltó en la negociación.

items.pregunta: We need to carefully ___ the risks before we sign the contract.
items.explicacion_es: "Assess" significa evaluar, y es lo que debes hacer con los riesgos antes de firmar.

items.pregunta: Sales have fallen ___ since the new competitor entered the market.
items.explicacion_es: "Fall sharply" es la colocación natural para decir que algo bajó de forma brusca, mientras que "hardly" significa "apenas".

items.pregunta: The manager said the proposal was "feasible." What did she mean?
items.explicacion_es: "Feasible" significa factible o viable, es decir, que se puede llevar a cabo en la práctica.

items.pregunta: The project looks simple, but ___ it will take several months to complete.
items.explicacion_es: "Actually" significa "en realidad" y no "actualmente", que en inglés se dice "currently".

items.pregunta: The client phoned to ___ the meeting because of a family emergency.
items.explicacion_es: "Call off" significa cancelar, que es lo que hace el cliente con la reunión.

items.pregunta: If I ___ about the strike, I would have booked a different flight.
items.explicacion_es: En el tercer condicional usas "if" + past perfect ("had known") para hablar de una situación pasada que no ocurrió.

items.pregunta: By the time the client arrives, we ___ the presentation.
items.explicacion_es: Con "by the time" usas el futuro perfecto para indicar que una acción estará terminada antes de un momento futuro.

items.pregunta: The new software, ___ was installed last week, keeps crashing.
items.explicacion_es: En una cláusula relativa no especificativa, que va entre comas, debes usar "which" y no "that".

items.pregunta: I'm not used to ___ so early, but my new job requires it.
items.explicacion_es: Después de "be used to" usas el verbo en -ing porque "to" funciona como preposición.

items.pregunta: When the director asked for the report, it ___ to the client.
items.explicacion_es: Necesitas la voz pasiva en past perfect porque el informe recibió la acción antes de otro momento del pasado.

items.pregunta: She suggested ___ the deadline by one week.
items.explicacion_es: Después de "suggest" usas el verbo en -ing, y nunca "to" + infinitivo ni objeto + infinitivo.

items.audio_en: A: Did you get a chance to look at the budget I sent you? B: I did. Most of the figures look fine, but I'm not sure the marketing section is realistic. We'd be spending twice what we spent last year, and there's no clear plan for measuring the results.
items.pregunta: What is the second speaker's main concern?
opciones: The budget arrived too late to review.
Most of the figures contain mistakes.
The marketing spending has no clear way to measure results.
Last year's marketing campaign was unsuccessful.
items.explicacion_es: La persona dice que el gasto en marketing se duplica sin un plan claro para medir los resultados.

items.audio_en: Hi Sarah, it's Tom from the travel agency. I'm afraid the hotel you wanted is fully booked for those dates. However, I've found a similar one about ten minutes away, and it's actually a bit cheaper. Could you call me back by Thursday so I can confirm the reservation?
items.pregunta: Why is Tom calling Sarah?
opciones: To offer her an alternative hotel.
To tell her the prices have gone up.
items.explicacion_es: Tom llama porque el hotel original está lleno y le propone otro similar y más barato.

items.audio_en: A: So, how did the interview go? B: Well, they seemed impressed with my experience, but they kept asking whether I'd be willing to relocate. A: And would you? B: Honestly, I'd never really thought about moving, so I didn't give them a clear answer.
items.pregunta: What can we understand from the conversation?
opciones: The interviewers were not interested in B's experience.
B refused to move to another city.
B has already accepted the job offer.
B is unsure about relocating for the job.
items.explicacion_es: La persona admite que nunca había pensado en mudarse y no dio una respuesta clara, así que está indecisa.

items.audio_en: Good morning, everyone. Before we begin, there's been a change to the schedule. The session on digital marketing, originally planned for this afternoon, has been moved to tomorrow morning because the speaker's flight was cancelled. In its place, we'll hold an open discussion on remote work. Lunch will be served at the usual time.
items.pregunta: What will happen this afternoon?
opciones: An open discussion on remote work.
Nothing, because the event is cancelled.
items.explicacion_es: El anuncio dice que la sesión de marketing digital pasa a mañana y que en su lugar habrá una discusión sobre trabajo remoto.

items.pregunta: Despite the setback, the team remained ___ and delivered the project on time.
items.explicacion_es: "Resilient" describe a alguien que se recupera de las dificultades y sigue adelante, lo cual encaja con entregar el proyecto a tiempo pese al contratiempo.

items.pregunta: The proposal was rejected because the costs far ___ the potential benefits.
items.explicacion_es: "Outweigh" significa superar en peso o importancia, y es la colocación natural para comparar costos y beneficios.

items.pregunta: Our sales figures have been ___ lately: one month they're up, the next they're down.
items.explicacion_es: "Erratic" significa irregular o impredecible; ten cuidado con los falsos amigos "eventual" (final), "actual" (real) y "sensible" (sensato).

items.pregunta: The negotiations reached a ___ when neither side was willing to compromise.
items.explicacion_es: "Stalemate" es un punto muerto o estancamiento, lo que ocurre cuando ninguna de las partes cede.

items.pregunta: When asked about possible layoffs, the manager gave a rather evasive answer. What does "evasive" mean here?
items.explicacion_es: "Evasive" significa evasivo, es decir, que evita responder de forma directa o clara.

items.pregunta: We need to carefully ___ the risks before committing to the investment.
items.explicacion_es: "Assess" significa evaluar; "assist" es ayudar y "attend" es asistir a algo, dos confusiones frecuentes entre hispanohablantes.

items.pregunta: ___ I known about the delay, I would have rebooked my flight.
items.explicacion_es: En el tercer condicional con inversión se omite "if" y se pone "had" antes del sujeto: "Had I known...".

items.pregunta: Not only ___ the deadline, but they also went over budget.
items.explicacion_es: Después de "Not only" al inicio de la oración se usa inversión con auxiliar: "did they miss".

items.pregunta: It's high time we ___ a decision about the new supplier.
items.explicacion_es: Con "It's high time" se usa el pasado simple para referirse al presente e indicar que algo ya debería estar ocurriendo.

items.pregunta: The report, ___ conclusions were widely criticized, was eventually withdrawn.
items.explicacion_es: "Whose" expresa posesión en una cláusula relativa (las conclusiones del informe); "that" no se usa en cláusulas no especificativas.

items.pregunta: She must ___ the email; otherwise, she would have replied by now.
items.explicacion_es: Para hacer una deducción negativa sobre el pasado se usa "must not have" + participio.

items.pregunta: I'd rather you ___ the client until we've finalized the figures.
items.explicacion_es: Con "I'd rather" + otro sujeto se usa el pasado simple para expresar una preferencia sobre el presente o el futuro.

items.audio_en: A: So, what did you think of Mark's presentation? B: Well, the slides were certainly colorful. And he did manage to fill the whole hour. A: That's one way of putting it. B: Let's just say I'm still not sure what he was proposing.
items.pregunta: What does speaker B imply about the presentation?
opciones: It was too short to cover the topic.
It was very impressive and persuasive.
It looked good but lacked real substance.
items.explicacion_es: B solo elogia aspectos superficiales y admite que no entendió la propuesta, lo que implica que la presentación carecía de contenido.

items.audio_en: Hi Laura, it's Tom from procurement. I know we penciled in Thursday to go over the supplier contracts, but legal still haven't signed off on the revised terms, so there's not much point meeting until they do. I'll chase them this afternoon and get back to you with a new date, hopefully early next week. In the meantime, if you could hold off on contacting the suppliers, that would be great.
items.pregunta: What does Tom ask Laura to do?
opciones: Wait before getting in touch with the suppliers
items.explicacion_es: "Hold off on contacting the suppliers" significa esperar antes de contactar a los proveedores.

items.audio_en: A: I heard you were thinking about taking the job in Singapore. B: I was, but the more I looked into it, the less sense it made. The salary's higher on paper, but once you factor in housing costs, I'd actually be worse off. Plus, they wanted me to start next month, which just isn't realistic.
items.pregunta: Why is speaker B probably not taking the job?
opciones: The salary offered is lower than B's current one.
B doesn't want to live abroad.
It wouldn't pay off financially, and the start date is too soon.
items.explicacion_es: B explica que, por el costo de la vivienda, ganaría menos en términos reales y que empezar el mes próximo no es realista.

items.audio_en: Before we wrap up, a quick word about the quarterly figures. On the face of it, they look encouraging: revenue is up eight percent. But I'd urge a bit of caution. Most of that growth came from a single one-off contract, and if you strip that out, we're essentially flat. So let's not get carried away just yet.
items.pregunta: What is the speaker's main point?
opciones: The growth is misleading because it depends on one exceptional deal.
The team should celebrate the excellent results.
The one-off contract has been cancelled.
items.explicacion_es: El hablante advierte que el crecimiento se debe a un solo contrato excepcional y que, sin él, los resultados están estancados.

items.pregunta: The CEO's statement was deliberately ___, leaving analysts unsure whether the merger would actually go ahead.
items.explicacion_es: "Equivocal" significa ambiguo o poco claro a propósito, lo que explica por qué los analistas quedaron con dudas.

items.pregunta: In the sentence "The quarterly report glosses over the financial risks of the expansion", what does "glosses over" mean?
opciones: deals with superficially to avoid drawing attention
items.explicacion_es: "Gloss over" significa tratar algo de forma superficial para que no se note o no se discuta a fondo.

items.pregunta: We can't afford to be ___ about data security; a single breach could ruin our reputation.
items.explicacion_es: "Complacent" significa confiado en exceso o descuidado, que es justo la actitud que no te puedes permitir con la seguridad de los datos.

items.pregunta: The new director's arrival proved to be the ___ for a complete overhaul of the department.
items.explicacion_es: "Catalyst" es algo o alguien que provoca o acelera un cambio importante.

items.pregunta: It was rather ___ of him to claim he hadn't seen the email, given that he had actually replied to it.
items.explicacion_es: "Disingenuous" significa poco sincero o que finge ignorancia, mientras que "ingenuous" significa ingenuo y no encaja en el contexto.

items.pregunta: Let's not ___ hairs over the exact wording; the substance of the contract is perfectly acceptable.
items.explicacion_es: La expresión fija "split hairs" significa fijarse en detalles insignificantes o discutir por minucias.

items.pregunta: ___ had the contract been signed than the client started asking for changes.
items.explicacion_es: Solo "No sooner" se combina con "than" en esta inversión, porque "Hardly", "Scarcely" y "Barely" van seguidos de "when".

items.pregunta: Were it not ___ your timely intervention, the deal would almost certainly have collapsed.
items.explicacion_es: La estructura condicional invertida "Were it not for..." equivale a "si no hubiera sido por...".

items.pregunta: So ___ the public backlash that the company withdrew the advert within hours.
items.explicacion_es: Cuando una oración empieza con "So + adjetivo", el verbo va antes del sujeto: "So fierce was the backlash that...".

items.pregunta: ___ the circumstances, I think we handled the client's complaint remarkably well.
items.explicacion_es: "Given" funciona como preposición con el sentido de "teniendo en cuenta" y es la única opción correcta delante de un sustantivo.

items.pregunta: Much ___ I admire her ambition, I simply can't support her proposal in its current form.
items.explicacion_es: "Much as" es una estructura concesiva fija que significa "por mucho que" o "aunque".

items.pregunta: I'd rather you ___ the figures to the client until we've double-checked them.
items.explicacion_es: Después de "I'd rather" + otro sujeto se usa el pasado simple con valor de presente o futuro, por eso es "didn't send".

items.audio_en: On paper, Daniel is an outstanding candidate. His CV is impressive, and he clearly knows the industry inside out. In the interview, though, he kept asking who he'd be reporting to and how often he'd get feedback. He seemed rather unsettled when I mentioned that our project leads largely set their own priorities. I'm just not convinced he'd thrive in a team where nobody really holds your hand.
items.pregunta: What does the speaker imply about Daniel?
opciones: He lacks the necessary industry knowledge.
He was too confident during the interview.
He might struggle to work without close supervision.
He would prefer a more senior position.
items.explicacion_es: La hablante sugiere que Daniel necesita mucha orientación y que tal vez no se adapte a un equipo donde se trabaja con autonomía.

items.audio_en: A: So, are we renewing the contract with Hartley's? B: Well, their prices are competitive, I'll give them that. And when they deliver on time, the quality is excellent. A: When they deliver on time? B: Let's just say I've had to rearrange the production schedule more often than I'd like. I'd want some firm guarantees in writing before we sign anything.
items.pregunta: What is the second speaker's position on renewing the contract?
opciones: She is strongly against renewing it under any conditions.
She would renew it only if the supplier commits to reliable delivery.
She thinks the supplier's prices are too high.
She is concerned mainly about the quality of the products.
items.explicacion_es: La hablante reconoce las ventajas del proveedor, pero da a entender que solo renovaría con garantías por escrito sobre la puntualidad de las entregas.

items.audio_en: A: So, what did you think of my presentation for the board? B: Well, you've obviously put a tremendous amount of work into it, and the slides are beautifully designed. I did wonder, though, whether the board would have the patience for forty-odd slides. They tend to make up their minds in the first ten minutes. You might find they respond better to something a little more streamlined.
items.pregunta: What is the second speaker suggesting?
opciones: The presentation should be considerably shorter.
The slides need a more professional design.
The presentation needs more supporting data.
The board meeting should be rescheduled.
items.explicacion_es: El hablante elogia el trabajo, pero insinúa con tacto que cuarenta diapositivas son demasiadas y que conviene acortar la presentación.

items.audio_en: The website described the hotel as being within easy reach of the city centre. Technically, I suppose that was true, provided you didn't mind two buses and a forty-minute walk. To be fair, the room itself was spotless, and the staff couldn't have been more helpful. Still, next time I think I'll pay a bit more and spare myself the daily commute.
items.pregunta: What does the speaker imply about the hotel?
opciones: The staff were unfriendly and unhelpful.
The room was not as clean as advertised.
It was more expensive than other hotels in the area.
Its location had been described in a misleading way.
items.explicacion_es: El hablante da a entender con ironía que la descripción de la ubicación era engañosa, aunque elogia la habitación y al personal.
